coarse_request: Please design a luxury airplane manufacturing process that includes the roles of 'customer', 'warehouse employees', 'sales', 'engineer', 'manufacturing teams', and 'test flight crew'. The key activities are 'receiving customer order', 'manufacturing parts', 'assembling interior', and 'performing test flight', and there should be decision points regarding 'parts availability' and 'OEE threshold'.
fine_grained_text:
Step 1: An order to cash process starts when a customer order is received.
After the order has been processed, it is sent to the warehouse.
The warehouse employees determine the parts required to produce the requested items.
If any parts are not available in the warehouse, these are ordered.
Once all necessary parts are available, production will start.
After production, quality checks will be performed.
If the production process has finished, products will be packaged and labeled, before returning to the warehouse.
Finally, sales will be informed about the completed production and the product can be sold to the customer.
[Transition]: Based on the provided processes, there is no direct causal link between the outcome of Process A (finished goods) and the initiation of Process B (machine monitoring). However, assuming Process A describes a manufacturing phase and Process B describes the monitoring of the equipment used during that phase, the following transition connects them logically:

**Once production begins in Process A, Process B is triggered to monitor the machinery's performance, ensuring efficiency and halting operations if the OEE drops below the required threshold.**
Step 2: Title: OEE

Write a process, that collects relevant information from a machine, and calculated the Overall Equipment Efficiency (OEE).
If the OEE falls below a certain value/percentage, stop the machine and send an email to an engineer.
When the machine is restarted, continue measuring.
When the machine is disconnected, stop the process.
[Transition]: If the OEE-monitored machine is the one manufacturing parts for the luxury airplane, a shutdown triggered by low efficiency would halt production, preventing those components from being sent to the assembly team and delaying Process B.
Step 3: Title: Luxury Airplane

You produce airplanes.
While the base model is always the same, your customer likes to pimp their airplane with fancy interior.
You let them decide between a number of 5 different bars, the number of seats, their color, and the amount of water in the toilets of their plane (you can come up with additional stuff).
After you received the specifications you send the requirements to different teams to manufacture the parts.
E.g. manufacturing the vodka bar is done by the Russian team, the whiskey bar is manufactured by an Irish team.
After receiving the individual bits and pieces, the interior of the plane is assembled, and the plane is sent on a test flight.
During the flight you create a test protocol which is sent to you and the customer.
The plane is delivered to the customer, which has to confirm.
[Transition]: Upon delivery of the finished airplane, the customer uses the enclosed test protocol as the architectural plan to begin building a tree house.
Step 4: Title: Building a House

You want to build a tree house.
First you collect your requirements, and send them to a tree house architect.
The architect sends you back a draft, which you refine multiple times with additional requirements.
You then create the list of needed materials from the plan.
These materials fall into several categories, you order them from several online stores.
While the order is processed, you send messages to several of your friends to build the house.
After the house is built, you send invitations for a tree house party to your friends.
In order to buy the snacks for the party, a list of people that attend the party is created.
[Transition]: After the list of party attendees is created, the requirement for a custom chainsaw to prepare the wood for the event triggers Process B.
Step 5: Title: Chainsaw

You produce custom chainsaws on demand.
Your chainsaws have at least 5 properties such as length of the "guide bar" (Schwertlaenge), chain width, electric or motor chainsaw.
After your customer told you the properties, you can start ordering the parts from various online sources (in parallel).
After the parts arrive you have to do a manual inspection of all parts, and then assemble the parts.
During production, you regularly send updates to your customer.
After producing the first saw you send it to your customer.
If he likes it, the rest of his order are produced.
